title: IMF reports uneven global growth in its October outlook
sourceTitle: IMF reports uneven global growth in its October outlook

pages.text: The International Monetary Fund published news about the world economy in October. People often call this group the IMF. It studies growth, jobs, trade, and prices in many countries.
The IMF said the world economy was still growing. But growth was not the same in every country. Some countries had more chances to grow than other countries.

The IMF said investment in artificial intelligence was helping some economies. Other economies faced problems. Countries that needed to buy energy from other places were among those facing harder conditions.
The IMF also expected higher prices for some goods. Food and energy prices were important reasons. The report showed why families and leaders in different countries might face different challenges.

The International Monetary Fund presented its October World Economic Outlook with a warning about growing differences between national economies. It reported that global growth remained resilient despite a difficult international environment.

The IMF expected the world economy to expand by 3.1 percent in 2026 and by 3.4 percent in 2027. These forecasts described continuing growth, but the organisation stressed that the benefits were uneven.

Some economies were benefiting from rising investment connected to artificial intelligence and favourable trading conditions. In contrast, energy-importing and lower-income countries faced a more challenging outlook.

The IMF expected near-term inflation to reach 4.7 percent in 2026, partly because of higher food and energy prices. Its assessment drew attention to the different pressures experienced across the global economy.

In its October assessment, the International Monetary Fund characterised global economic performance as resilient yet increasingly divergent. Overall growth projections, it suggested, obscured significant differences in the conditions confronting individual economies.

The Fund forecast global expansion of 3.1 percent in 2026 and 3.4 percent in 2027. These headline projections pointed to continued activity without implying that the resulting gains would be distributed evenly.

Economies benefiting from investment driven by artificial intelligence or advantageous terms of trade appeared relatively well placed. Energy-importing countries and lower-income economies, meanwhile, faced more difficult circumstances.

The IMF also anticipated inflation of 4.7 percent in 2026, largely reflecting higher energy and food prices. Its message was that aggregate resilience should not conceal the unequal burdens associated with those pressures.

title: UN Security Council discusses violence in Gaza and the West Bank
sourceTitle: UN Security Council discusses violence in Gaza and the West Bank
license: SAGA original educational adaptation; linked source credited
attribution: SAGA educational summary based on United Nations information
editorialState: Original source-linked educational summary; consult original reporting for details

pages.text: The United Nations Security Council held a meeting in October. Its members talked about the Middle East. The meeting focused on Gaza and the West Bank, where many people were facing serious problems.
The United Nations reported more deadly strikes and violence in these areas. It also reported that more buildings were being destroyed. These events were part of the reason for the meeting.
The Security Council held an open debate. This is a kind of meeting where countries can discuss important problems. The situation in Gaza and the West Bank was the main subject.

The UN report described a difficult situation for people in the affected areas. The meeting showed that the conflict was still a major international concern. It did not mean that the problems had ended.

The United Nations Security Council held an open debate on the situation in the occupied Palestinian territory in October. The discussion focused particularly on recent developments in Gaza and the West Bank.
The UN reported an increase in deadly strikes, demolitions and other violence. Its account described these developments as the immediate background to the debate among Security Council participants.
An open debate provides a formal opportunity for countries to discuss international issues. In this case, the meeting brought attention to the conditions facing people in Gaza and the West Bank.

The UN report connected the discussion to rising violence and the destruction of buildings. It did not suggest that holding the debate had already resolved the conflict or changed the situation on the ground.
The United Nations Security Council convened an open debate concerning the occupied Palestinian territory, with particular attention to developments in Gaza and the West Bank during October.

The UN described an escalation in lethal strikes, demolitions and violence as the immediate context for the diplomatic discussion. Its reporting distinguished developments on the ground from the international response to them.

By placing the situation before the Council, the debate provided a formal forum for considering a matter of international concern. The existence of such a discussion should not be mistaken for an agreed resolution.

The UN account underscored the continued international significance of developments in Gaza and the West Bank. It documented the focus of the meeting without claiming that conditions for those affected had already improved.
